newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey to hold its line on NATO expansion veto.
newsitem.headline: Turkey to hold its line on NATO expansion veto.

text.p: Turkey is ready to repeat warnings that it could block the expansion of NATO during the defence alliance's talks this week, the foreign ministry said on Monday.
"When this agenda item is taken up and when required, these views of the Turkish government will be repeated," ministry spokesman Omer Akbel told a news briefing.
Turkey has threatened to veto the eastward expansion of NATO if the European Union does not forge closer ties with Ankara.

Akbel said Turkey's foreign minister, Tansu Ciller, was likely to tell the meeting of NATO foreign ministers in Brussels on Tuesday that membership in the military pact and the EU were closely linked. New U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright will be at the meeting.
State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said on Sunday that Washington was confident Turkey's objections would not stand in the way of eastern European countries joining NATO.
"We believe NATO enlargement will go ahead on the 7th and 8th of July and that is the will of all the NATO countries," he told journalists in Germany.
Albright arrived in Europe at the weekend at the start of her first foreign trip since becoming secretary of state last month.
